blocks.text: The hexagonal frame work of benzene ring can be conveniently explained by using hybridization approach. According to this, each carbon atom in benzene is sp² hybridized. The three sp² hybrid orbitals on each carbon are utilized to form three σ-bonds, two with adjacent carbon atoms and one with a hydrogen atom. Since all the sp² orbitals are in the same plane, therefore, all the carbon and hydrogen atoms of this σ framework are coplanar at 120°.

The six unhybrid '2p' orbitals, one from each carbon, are perpendicular to this sigma framework and parallel to each other overlap sideways to form a π-electron cloud above and below the plane of the benzene ring making it a conjugated molecule. Due to this overlap six electrons are shared equally among all the six carbons and this is known as delocalization of π electron.
This delocalization causes all the six C - C bond lengths to be same (139 pm). Benzene is thus represented as a hexagon with a circle inscribed, where the circle represents delocalized π electrons.

blocks.alt: Three panels. (a) Sigma framework: six carbons in a hexagon, each C-C bond formed by two overlapping sp2 lobes and each C-H bond by an sp2 lobe overlapping the H orbital; labels sp2-sp2 C-C sigma bond and sp2-s C-H sigma bond. (b) The ring in perspective with a p orbital (two lobes) above and below each carbon and dashed lines showing their sideways overlap. (c) The delocalised pi cloud as two rings above and below the C6H6 skeleton.

items: The delocalization (resonance) energy of benzene is about 152 kJ mol⁻¹. Explain what that means and how it affects the reactivity of benzene.
